subject: Immediate hotpatch deployed for runtime compaction issue — customer guidance
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Liu <jordan.liu@acme.ai>, ops@acme.ai
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Immediate hotpatch deployed for runtime compaction issue — customer guidance

Hi Jordan / Acme ops team,

We deployed an unscheduled hotpatch at 09:05 PDT to address a memory-growth issue in our runtime's KV compaction path that, under a small subset of long-lived streams, could cause degraded throughput and increased tail latency. The fix was targeted, validated on staging, and rolled to your dedicated nodes in region us-west-2 at 09:05.

What this means for you
- Impact window: 2027-07-19 08:50–09:05 PDT. Any in-flight requests during that window may have experienced elevated latency or transient 5xx errors.
- Action required: none mandatory. If you run long-lived worker processes that pin model contexts, we recommend restarting them once in the next maintenance window (see verification steps below).
- Rollback: We hold a rollback plan (INC-7891) in case any regressions surface. We will coordinate if rollback becomes necessary.

Verification steps (recommended, quick)
1) Run the attached verify_kv_check.sh against one worker (sh verify_kv_check.sh) — it returns a 200 and a short payload when KV compaction is healthy.
2) Send a small prompt suite (example in script) and confirm median latency is within 1.5x of normal.
3) If you see persistent 5xxs or elevated latencies after restart, reply and we will escalate immediately.

Attachments: hotfix_20270719.patch (patch diff), verify_kv_check.sh (quick verification script), incident_runbook_excerpt.pdf

We will follow up with a short postmortem and any credit/SLAs items if the incident meets thresholds. Apologies for the short notice; this was an emergency push to prevent broader degradation.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Liu <jordan.liu@acme.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, ops@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 09:21:36 -0700
Subject: Re: Immediate hotpatch deployed for runtime compaction issue — customer guidance

Thanks Irene — quick questions:
1) Did the hotpatch touch any customer data paths or only the compaction routine?
2) For our long-lived workers: do you recommend restart now or wait for a scheduled window? We have a heavy batch tonight.
3) Will this incident be eligible for SLA credit? Our SRE needs a timeline for internal reporting.

We ran a couple of test prompts and saw one spike to 1.8s median (normally ~0.35s). Hoping that’s expected behavior during the window.

—Jordan
Platform Engineering, Acme AI
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Liu <jordan.liu@acme.ai>, ops@acme.ai
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 09:30:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Immediate hotpatch deployed for runtime compaction issue — customer guidance

Hi Jordan — quick answers inline.

On Mon, Jul 19, 2027 at 9:21 AM Jordan Liu <jordan.liu@acme.ai> wrote:
> 1) Did the hotpatch touch any customer data paths or only the compaction routine?

Only the compaction routine and internal memory housekeeping. No customer payloads or persisted embeddings were modified. The change is a defensive bounds-check and GC timing adjustment.

> 2) For our long-lived workers: do you recommend restart now or wait for a scheduled window? We have a heavy batch tonight.

If you have a heavy batch tonight, delay restart until after your batch completes. The patch is live on the node side and will not retroactively affect already-initialized KV contexts — that's why a restart of long-lived workers will fully realize the memory/latency fix. If you prefer we can schedule a rolling restart to reduce impact; tell us which hostnames to target and we’ll coordinate.

> 3) Will this incident be eligible for SLA credit?

We will evaluate under our SLA policy. Based on preliminary telemetry the impact window was short and affected a subset of streams; we'll determine credit eligibility in the postmortem. I’ll flag this for our finance/renewals team.

About your observed spike: 1.8s during the window aligns with the elevated tail we saw internally. If you continue to see >1.0s medians after your planned restart, please attach the verify output and we’ll open an elevated debugging call.

—Irene
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>

Note: keep INC-7891 open for follow-up and link logs in the postmortem.

Thanks — Markus
VP, Customer Reliability
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Liu <jordan.liu@acme.ai>, ops@acme.ai
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: brief postmortem and next steps (INC-7891)

Hi Jordan — thank you for the quick coordination yesterday and for running the verification. Attached is a brief postmortem (postmortem-acme-20270720.pdf) and the runbook excerpt we referenced. Summary points:

1) Root cause: under a long-lived, high-prefix-diversity workload the compaction timing could defer GC and trigger unbounded memory growth in the KV compaction routine.
2) Impact: short period of elevated tail latency and transient 5xxs for a subset (~2%) of streams between 08:50–09:05 PDT on 2027-07-19.
3) Mitigation: hotpatch applied to node binary to add tighter bounds checks and an earlier compaction kick. Nodes in Acme's dedicated pool were patched at 09:05 PDT.
4) Customer actions: recommend rolling restart of long-lived workers when convenient (not required). We flagged your account for priority review re: SLA credits; Vanessa will reach out with proposed language.

We have created JIRA INC-7891 and posted full logs and the longer postmortem here: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/postmortems/postmortem-acme-20270720

If you'd like a short review call, I have openings tomorrow 10:00–11:00 or Thursday 14:00–15:00 PDT. Please pick a time and we’ll send a calendar invite.

Apologies again for the disruption and thank you for your patience. We will follow up with any SLA/credit resolutions.

Best,
Irene Choi
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
